description: "Use when designing or implementing the replacement .NET backend: model/database/entity design, endpoint contracts, application services, authorization, exact money, persistence, migrations, and durable jobs."
applyTo: "backend/**"
---
# Backend

- Follow [application boundaries](../../docs/ADR/ADR-0002-application-boundaries.md) and [shared-instance access](../../docs/ADR/ADR-0003-shared-instance-access.md). Enforce authorization and input validation in the backend, including SSR data access.
- Follow the evaluated [foundation stack](../../docs/ADR/ADR-0007-application-foundation.md) and [reproducible commands](../../docs/development.md). Use the root solution and its pinned NuGet/SDK configuration.
- Keep domain/application behavior independent of Angular and Azure SDK entities. Define explicit API contracts and stable error codes, not raw exception messages for display.
- Follow [backend project boundaries](../../docs/ADR/ADR-0017-backend-project-boundaries.md): `PocketMonkey.Host` owns runtime composition, application behavior, security, and filesystem lifecycle; `PocketMonkey.Storage` owns persisted entities, context/mappings, and migrations. Only Host references Storage; do not introduce a reverse dependency or routine repository wrappers.
- Use meaningful names and separate interface files. Respect inherited EditorConfig rules; do not introduce primary constructors against the existing preference.
- Use exact money arithmetic, with the representation/rounding agreed before financial implementation. Post entries and stored balance updates atomically; enforce idempotency and concurrency guarantees in the selected persistence layer.
- Preserve financial audit history with explicit corrections. EF Core SQLite is selected; currency/precision, negative balances, retention, and job catch-up policies remain decisions for their responsible phases, not assumptions to hard-code now.
- Use immutable internal user IDs and UTC timestamps. Apply the validated IANA timezone from Docker ENV `TZ` explicitly for business periods; UI language must not change those periods.
- Make scheduled work durable, retry-safe, and observable. Do not hold database transactions across network/filesystem operations or rely on timers firing exactly once.
- Keep credentials and persistent authentication keys private. Validate configuration/permissions before readiness; log failures without passwords, cookies, or private payloads.
- Keep projects within the root NuGet/build configuration. Restore locked dependencies and build from the repository root so its SDK pin is applied.
- Keep all EF migration implementations, designer metadata, and the single model snapshot directly in `backend/PocketMonkey.Storage/Migrations`, using namespace `PocketMonkey.Storage.Migrations`. Before generating, inspect the existing history/snapshot and use the exact scoped command in the foundation guide, targeting Storage with Host as `--startup-project`, explicit `--output-dir Migrations`, and `--namespace PocketMonkey.Storage.Migrations`. Never generate a second migration folder or snapshot. Run the migration-layout guard and a real populated-schema upgrade check after generation or relocation; preserve existing migration IDs and operations.
- Verify user-facing behavior through E2E tests; use focused real-persistence integration tests for rollback, constraints, migrations, concurrency, and controlled job failures. Do not add routine mock/unit suites or coverage quotas.

## Design Review Gate

- Use the combined [backend/data design workflow](../skills/backend-data-design/SKILL.md) before adding or changing entities, relationships, persisted fields, constraints/indexes, migrations, endpoint routes/contracts, authorization visibility, or application/hosted-service responsibilities. This applies to design proposals as well as implementation.
- Summarize the anticipated design in the applicable migration plan: purpose/invariants, affected class names and namespaces with file links, data and API changes, populated-data implications, applicable ADRs/conflicts, and focused real-stack acceptance checks. Clearly distinguish existing types from proposed types and unresolved policies from agreed decisions.
- Mark the proposal with a revision identifier. Wait for explicit approval identifying the current backend/data design proposal before changing implementation or generating migrations. Record the approval, date, and reviewed scope in that plan. Feedback, corrections, policy acceptance alone, a generic "proceed", or passing checks do not approve a design revision. Preserve previous approvals as history; material revisions require fresh approval, without repeatedly asking while review is ongoing.
- Identify the authoritative ADR for each affected topic; add a new record only for a genuinely distinct topic or justified topic split. Obtain agreement on architectural conflicts before implementation, then update accepted enduring decisions under [ADR-0001](../../docs/ADR/ADR-0001-architecture-decision-records.md), the index and affected links. Keep the topic's ADR number/filename stable and record significant changes with dated rationale, retaining complete earlier wording in Git. Unresolved ADR proposals remain in plans.
- Formatting, test-only changes, and behavior-preserving fixes within an approved design do not require a new proposal. If a fix changes schema, contracts, authorization, business invariants, or responsibilities, the gate applies. Do not use this exception to bypass review or treat this instruction change as approval of any future backend design.
